scope: Bounded RP2350 Arm target knowledge, not an exhaustive ISA database, executable cost model or hardware timing qualification.

facts.claim: RP2350 implements Armv8-M Main, Security and DSP extensions, single-precision FP arithmetic and double-precision FP load/store, with normal execution in halfword-aligned 16/32-bit Thumb instructions.
conditions: Use RP2350 configuration, not the superset of instructions described by the architecture manual.

facts.claim: The chip configuration has DSP and single-precision FPU support, but explicitly has no MTB and does not use CDE modules.
conditions: Generic optional core features and v8.1-M manual coverage do not establish device support.

facts.claim: ADD immediate T1 is 16-bit with low-register Rd/Rn and unsigned imm3; T2 is 16-bit, destructive low-register Rdn with unsigned imm8. Both select flag updates outside an IT block.
conditions: T1 immediate 0..7; T2 immediate 0..255.
Flag liveness and IT context must be preserved; the encodings are not generic non-flag-setting three-address ADD replacements.

facts.claim: ADD immediate T3 is a 32-bit modified-immediate form with an S bit; T4/ADDW uses an unsigned 12-bit plain immediate and does not update flags.
conditions: T4 immediate 0..4095.
Ordinary-data use excludes SP/PC and their related encodings; retain the documented register restrictions.
Width suffix and flag behavior are separate properties.

facts.claim: ADD register T1 is a 16-bit low-register three-address form with IT-dependent flag updates; T2 is a 16-bit destructive form with extended register fields and no flag updates.
conditions: T2 destination also supplies the first operand.
Use ordinary R0-R12 only here; SP/PC alias and control-flow restrictions are outside this starter rule.

facts.claim: MOV immediate T1 is 16-bit with low Rd and imm8, selecting flag updates outside IT; wide T2 has an independent S bit and modified immediate.
conditions: T1 immediate 0..255.
Do not replace a non-flag-setting constant construction if live condition flags would change.
Do not assume the carry behavior of every modified immediate is identical.

facts.claim: MOV register T1 has 16-bit extended register fields and does not update flags; not all compact instructions require low registers.
conditions: Ordinary-data copy rule excludes SP/PC and related restrictions.
Do not substitute the distinct shifted/flag-setting T2 encoding indiscriminately.

facts.claim: LDR literal T1 uses low Rt and a positive imm8 scaled by four, reaching 0..1020 bytes from Align(PC,4); T2 is wide and reaches -4095..4095 bytes from that architectural base.
conditions: Restrict this rule to ordinary register loads; PC destinations introduce control-flow and alignment rules.
Check final addresses, architectural PC interpretation and encoding size, not source-text distance.

facts.claim: Supported single unaligned accesses in Normal memory split into aligned bus transactions; Device-memory unaligned accesses fault, and double/multiple accesses require word alignment.
conditions: CCR.UNALIGN_TRP can make otherwise supported unaligned accesses fault.
Cross-memory-map-boundary unaligned accesses are not a safe optimization.
Do not infer permission to widen volatile/MMIO accesses.

facts.claim: The datasheet execution timings describe a limited, non-exceptional measured sample with one running core, no cache misses and no active DMA, not universal per-opcode guarantees.
conditions: Instruction fetch, memory waits, exceptions, other-core and DMA contention can change observed costs.

facts.claim: Most simple ALU operations execute in one cycle; non-simple shifted operands and certain expanded immediates can add a result-use penalty. Complex flag-setting forms incur the penalty even with an independent following instruction.
conditions: Simple shifted-operand cases are LSL #0..3.
Do not generalize this classification to every opcode or ignore S/implicit flag effects.

facts.claim: Plain imm12 ADD/SUB, immediate MOV/MOVS, UBFX/SBFX/BFI and simple standalone shifts are documented exceptions without the complex-ALU result-use penalty.
conditions: Preserve exact legal instruction form and operand semantics.
The absence of this dependency penalty does not exclude fetch or memory stalls.

facts.claim: Multiply/multiply-accumulate issue in one cycle but have a one-cycle result delay. Multiplier operands are required at cycle n, the accumulate operand at n+1 and the result at n+2.
conditions: Different consumer operand positions can have different dependency costs.
A one-cycle issue rate is not one-cycle availability for arbitrary consumers.

facts.claim: The multiply result can feed a following multiply-accumulate's accumulate input without the ordinary result-use bubble in the documented cases.
conditions: The destination wording and alternating-destination examples must not be reduced to a destination-equality heuristic.
Verify exact MLA/long-multiply forms and operand positions in D02.

facts.claim: For documented ordinary divisions, n is the difference in highest-set-bit positions of operand magnitudes: n<0 takes two cycles; otherwise 4+floor(n/4), with a one-cycle immediate result-use penalty.
conditions: Use defined cases with nonzero dividend and divisor; highest-one position is undefined for zero. This formula does not establish divide-by-zero/trap behavior.
Signed magnitude, overflow edge cases and exceptional inputs need their own architectural/IR rules.

facts.claim: Loads take a cycle per loaded register plus possible delay; LDR's result and the last LDM/POP register have a result-use delay, except the PC case which has branch costs.
conditions: Address-generation registers are early source operands.
Other loaded registers do not inherit the last-register delay indiscriminately.
Memory can stall independently of the pipeline delay.

facts.claim: For the documented store result-use model, address-generation registers, including SP for PUSH, count as early sources; store data is not in that source class.
conditions: This is a scheduling distinction, not permission to ignore a store's data dependency.
The one-cycle store statement is not a general STM/PUSH register-count or bus-throughput model.

facts.claim: Documented branch timing is basic+2+L+U-(K&F) when taken and basic+1-F when not taken, with distinct loaded-PC, target-alignment and folding conditions.
conditions: Basic cost comes from the branch-producing instruction, including any load.
L/U/F/K are Boolean predicates defined in the topic note, not arbitrary fitted constants.
Final widths, addresses and dynamic folding history are needed.

facts.claim: The documented zero-cycle NOP folding uses opcode 0xBF00, not 0x46C0; a following 16-bit opcode can fold IT overhead, while condition-failed instructions inside IT still cost a cycle.
conditions: Previous-instruction folding requires its width, entry/alignment and not-already-folded predicates.
At most one cycle overlaps when two multi-cycle instructions fold.
NOP insertion is not automatically free in every path.

facts.claim: Core fetch bandwidth is 32 bits per cycle, but fetch and data access to the same downstream SRAM bank can contend; the nearby-literal example has a possible, not guaranteed, extra cycle.
conditions: Do not turn the example's modulo-16 distance into a universal fixed literal-load penalty.
Code location, prefetch position, bank mapping and other bus managers matter.

facts.claim: APSR N/Z/C/V are bits 31/30/29/28; Q is sticky saturation/overflow bit 27; GE bits 19..16 carry parallel arithmetic state consumed by SEL.
conditions: Q and GE availability depends on Main/DSP features.
Flag definitions and uses are instruction-specific; shifts, carry arithmetic and comparisons are not all identical.
APSR is not banked between security states; do not infer it is preserved on arbitrary transitions.

facts.claim: Base PCS uses r0-r3 for initial argument/result/scratch roles; r12 is scratch and may also be clobbered by a linker veneer.
conditions: Values and condition flags cannot be assumed live across arbitrary public calls.
This is not a claim that every composite/result fits those four registers.

facts.claim: Callees preserve r4-r8, r10, r11 and SP; r9's role is platform-specific and preservation depends on the PCS variant.
conditions: ABI-preserved does not mean available to allocation: retain frame, PHI, scratch and platform reservations.

facts.claim: N/Z/C/V/Q and GE condition/status bits are not preserved by the public interface contract; Q/GE modification also requires the feature to exist.
conditions: AAPCS's cross-architecture CPSR wording must not import unsupported A32 state/control bits into M33 APSR handling.

facts.claim: The stack is full-descending; SP stays within stack limits and word-aligned, and public interfaces additionally require SP modulo 8 to be zero.
conditions: Do not use an unallocated area below SP as an assumed red zone.
Saved registers, locals, outgoing arguments and interrupt frames are separate stack contributors.

facts.claim: Base argument marshaling uses r0-r3 then stack rules; double-word-aligned arguments round the next core register number to an even number, and hidden result addresses affect initial allocation.
conditions: Apply the complete staged marshaling rules, including composites and split/stack cases; do not count one register per C argument.

facts.claim: VFP register argument passing is a separate non-variadic PCS variant; variadic calls follow base marshaling. s16-s31/d8-d15 are preserved, while s0-s15/d0-d7 are scratch/argument/result registers.
conditions: Do not mix hard-float/base interfaces because the silicon has an FPU.
This describes applicable scalar register subsets, not proof of MVE/NEON support.

facts.claim: UNCROSS_I_D routes all instruction fetch to the Code port and load/store/debug accesses to the System port, unlike the generic core's address-based routing.
conditions: This removes the described internal routing conflict, not downstream AHB-bank contention.

facts.claim: SRAM totals 520 KiB in eight 64 KiB and two 4 KiB banks; the two main 256 KiB regions word-stripe across separate four-bank groups.
conditions: Logical contiguity does not imply one physical port.
Different managers can proceed in parallel only when bank/arbiter constraints permit.
Code placement must retain BSS, stack, startup-copy and other memory budgets.

facts.claim: The XIP cache is 16 KiB, two-way, with 8-byte lines and a documented one-cycle hit; it serves QSPI accesses, not all SRAM or peripheral memory.
conditions: A cache hit is not a whole-program CPI guarantee; misses, QMI configuration, arbitration and cold/warm state matter.
Secure/Non-secure cache access/maintenance permissions must be respected.

facts.claim: Coprocessor access needs Secure CPACR enablement or the appropriate Non-secure NSACR/CPACR_NS permissions; chip support alone is insufficient.
conditions: Actual application-entry register state has not been measured in D01.
GPIOC Non-secure accesses additionally follow GPIO access masks.

facts.claim: DCP uses canned multi-instruction CPU/coprocessor sequences, not a conventional full double-precision FPU; mantissa multiplication uses CPU long-multiply instructions.
conditions: Count transfers, CPU arithmetic, dependencies and context costs, not one cycle per C double operation.
Do not assume state persists between completed canned sequences.

facts.claim: DCP port 4 selects the current security state's instance; port 5 selects the Non-secure instance but is accessible only from Secure code. Interrupted engaged sequences need context handling.
conditions: The documented engaged-state save/restore protocol is necessary if an interrupt uses the same instance.

facts.claim: Standard DCP sequences flush subnormal input/output to zero and round nearest-even; fast division/square-root variants are not always correctly rounded.
conditions: Do not enable these sequences as a silent replacement for strict double semantics.
SDK benchmark figures and SDK helpers do not establish dependency-free compiler support.

facts.claim: FPv5 single-precision arithmetic uses overlapping S0-S31/D0-D15 views; double-word load/store capability is not double-precision arithmetic support.
conditions: FZ/DN modes alter subnormal/NaN handling; FP exceptions update status rather than providing FPU exception traps.
Do not reassociate arithmetic or split fused operations without preserving required rounding semantics.

facts.claim: Lazy FP stacking reserves an extended exception frame when FP context is active and delays saving FP state until needed; it does not eliminate stack demand.
conditions: Interrupt nesting, context state and handler FP use need explicit stack accounting before enabling FPU code.

facts.claim: Scalar VADD/VSUB/VMUL have one-cycle execution plus result delay; VMLA/VFMA occupy the FPU for three cycles and VDIV/VSQRT for fourteen, each with a result-delay qualification.
conditions: FP issue occupies the integer core for a cycle; later integer work and FPU readiness are distinct resources.
Same-accumulator forwarding and independent interleaving alter observed throughput.
Separate VMUL/VADD and fused VFMA are not generally rounding-equivalent.

facts.claim: Unstalled CDP/MCR/MCRR transfers have one-cycle costs; MRC/MRRC add result delay. A coprocessor can stall when not ready.
conditions: The ideal interface transfer rate is not the latency of an entire accelerated operation.
RCP delay variants and state/permission checks cannot be ignored.

facts.claim: GPIOC port 0 provides specific SIO GPIO operations; it is not an alternative implementation of every peripheral/MMIO load and store.
conditions: Preserve operation width, masks, simultaneous sampling and permitted security-state behavior.
Use explicit helpers only after their particular instruction mapping is verified.

facts.claim: RCP provides fault-detection/canary/validation mechanisms with seeded state and security-state-dependent behavior, not a generic arithmetic speedup.
conditions: Do not insert delay/security operations as a performance optimization or claim a security guarantee from instruction presence.

facts.claim: E27 miswires priority controls for APB/FASTPERI on the listed A2/A3/A4 revisions; ROM/SRAM/XIP priority controls are documented as correct.
conditions: Read the full priority mapping and both continuation pages before designing a contention experiment.
Actual badge revision is unresolved; no workaround is enabled here.

facts.claim: E11 clean-by-set/way can retag dirty XIP cache lines on listed A2/A3/A4 revisions; ordinary cache-hit cost is not permission to introduce arbitrary maintenance sequences.
conditions: Preserve the documented workaround if a future cold-cache experiment or runtime helper uses this operation.
Invalidate, clean and pin are not interchangeable operations.

facts.claim: E26 qualifies RCP delay use; the datasheet recommends non-delay variants and documents an A3 bootrom change.
conditions: Do not make a blanket security or deterministic-timing claim about RCP.
Hardware revision and actual boot/runtime state remain separate applicability questions.

facts.claim: The attached badges' silicon revisions, application-entry security/coprocessor state and cold/warm timing environment were not measured in D01.
conditions: Do not infer these from a target triple, working integer firmware or bootrom defaults.
Resolve through a separately qualified, non-destructive D02 observation before revision/state-dependent use.
